paper_metadata.title: Thermoplastic bonding of TiAl-based alloy and YSZ ceramic utilizing a Ni60Nb40 metallic glass as the filler metal

evidence.quote: Achieving a reliable bond between advanced ceramics and high-temperature application alloys for high-temperature applications can greatly enhance the operating temperature range of vital components like engines and turbines.

we have achieved success in bonding Yttria-stabilized zirconia (YSZ) ceramics with TiAl-base alloys through the use of a novel ceramic-metal joining method called thermoplastic bonding (TPB).

attributes.composition: Ti and Al with ratio close to 2:1

evidence.quote: The dark-gray block phase in zone I-layer I was marked as A in Fig. 3 (f). The EDS results show that phase A is mainly composed of Ti and Al with a ratio close to 2:1. Combine with the Ti-Al binary phase diagram, it can be inferred that phase A is AlTi2 [38].

attributes.location: zone I-layer I and zone I-layer II
attributes.composition: Al, Ti and Ni with ratio 2:1:1

evidence.quote: The gray matrix phase (marked as B) in zone I-layer II is mainly composed of Al, Ti and Ni, and the ratio is 2:1:1. Therefore, it is speculated that B is τ2-Al2NiTi.

attributes.morphology: phase surrounded by yellow dotted circle

evidence.quote: The phase surrounded by the yellow dotted circle (marked as I) was mainly composed of Al, Ti, and Ni. The size of phase I is relatively coarse, about 1–3 μm. The SAED patterns of phases I and L were shown in Fig. 5 (f) and (g), and these two phases can be identified as the FCC structure AlNi2Ti phase (PDF#19-0034) and the HCP structure AlNiNb phase (PDF#29-0060), respectively.

attributes.morphology: phase outlined by blue dotted line

evidence.quote: The phases outlined by the blue dotted line and the red dotted line are nanometer-sized, and they can be identified as the Al-Nb IMCs phase and the Ti-Ni IMCs phase according to the element distribution. The results of FFT show that J was the AlNb2 phase with tetragonal structure (PDF#14-0458) and K was the Ti2Ni phase with FCC structure (PDF#18-0898).

attributes.morphology: phase outlined by red dotted line

evidence.quote: The phases outlined by the blue dotted line and the red dotted line are nanometer-sized, and they can be identified as the Al-Nb IMCs phase and the Ti-Ni IMCs phase according to the element distribution. The results of FFT show that J was the AlNb2 phase with tetragonal structure (PDF#14-0458) and K was the Ti2Ni phase with FCC structure (PDF#18-0898).

The rest is the matrix phase (marked as L), which is outlined by a purple dotted line. Phase L is mainly composed of three elements: Al, Nb, and Ni. The SAED patterns of phases I and L were shown in Fig. 5 (f) and (g), and these two phases can be identified as the FCC structure AlNi2Ti phase (PDF#19-0034) and the HCP structure AlNiNb phase (PDF#29-0060), respectively.

attributes.location: zone II-layer I, zone II-layer II (matrix), zone II-layer III
attributes.composition: Ni and Nb, Nb higher than Ni

evidence.quote: The white-gray phases D (the white-gray phases in zone II-layer I), F (white-gray matrix phase in zone II-layer II), and G (the white-gray phases in zone II-layer III) have similar elemental compositions, so they should be the same phase. According to the EDS result and Ni-Nb binary phase diagram, it can be inferred that they are all Nb7Ni6 phases [38].

The ratio of Ni-Nb in the phase E (fine dark-gray block phases in zone II-layer II) is about 3:1, combined with the Ni-Nb binary phase diagram, it can be confirmed that it is the NbNi3 phase. Phases E and F in zone II-layer II constitute a typical eutectic microstructure.

evidence.section: 3.1 Filling behavior of MG on YSZ ceramic surface
evidence.quote: After the experiment, the deformed MG has been tested by XRD, and the image was shown in the lower left inset of Fig. 2 (a). The single broad peak indicates that the MG does not crystallize and maintains a whole amorphous structure, which proves that the whole filling process is carried out in the superliquid region of MG.

The typical microstructure and the corresponding elemental distribution maps of the YSZ/TiAl joint brazed at 1020°C for 60 min are shown in Fig. 3 (a) – (e). It can be seen that the joints are mainly composed of four parts: YSZ and TiAl substrate, zone I (diffusion-reaction zone adjacent to TiAl) and zone II (the crystallization of the amorphous zone in the middle area of the joint).

attributes.location: interface between YSZ ceramic and intermediate layer
attributes.cause: residual stress from thermal expansion coefficient mismatch

evidence.section: 3.3 Effect of holding temperature on the microstructure evolution of YSZ/TiAl joints
evidence.quote: It can be seen that there is a clear boundary at the interface between the YSZ ceramic and the intermediate layer, which is caused by interface cracking. Bonding or interdiffusion of non-reactive atoms with ceramics is very difficult [41]. Therefore, when the holding time is too short, the bonding of YSZ ceramic and Ni-Nb interlayer is insufficient, and the joint strength is relatively low. In this case, cracking occurred at the interface due to the residual stress generated by the thermal expansion coefficient mismatch.

evidence.section: 3.4 Mechanical property and fracture analysis of the YSZ/TiAl joint
evidence.quote: When the holding time is 30min, the shear strength is very low, only about 33 MPa, due to cracking at the interface between YSZ and the intermediate layer.

evidence.section: 3.4 Mechanical property and fracture analysis of the YSZ/TiAl joint
evidence.quote: It can be seen that the room temperature shear strength of the joint increases first and then decreases with the extension of the holding time, and reaches the highest value of about 141 MPa at 60min.
Remarkably, the TPB joint retains remarkable strength, with a value of approximately 84 MPa even when exposed to a high temperature of 600°C.

The method uses metallic glasses (MG) as an intermediate layer, and utilizes its superplastic deformation in the superliquid region to completely fill the rough surface of the base materials to achieve the same effect as liquid wetting [26–28], and then connect through the atomic diffusion between the filler and the base materials.

On the other hand, under high temperature and pressure for a long time, the atoms such as Ni, Nb in the intermediate layer will diffuse to a certain extent into the interior of the YSZ ceramic or bond with the atoms in the YSZ ceramic, thereby forming a good metallurgical bond [40].
